correctness.rationale: A factor must have 0, 2 or 4 ones. With 0 ones the even zero-runs contribute floor(M/2) distinct words. With 2 ones the disjoint cases are 11, flanked square 0^x110^x for 1<=x<=min(a,b) (the triple cluster cannot supply both flanks), and 10^b1 for even b. With 4 ones, two from each cluster forces 0^x11 0^b11 with x<=min(a,b) and x congruent to b mod 2 so a midpoint separates the clusters. One from the first and three from the second forces 10^b1110^b, present iff c>=b. All are literal factor contents, not occurrence or Parikh counts. For t=n-5 and m=min(a,b)>=1, t<=2M+m and the difference between the lower bound M/2+1/2+3m/2 and (2M+m+6)/4 is 5m/4-1>0. When m=0, a=0; even b gives at least floor(M/2)+3>floor((2M+6)/4), and odd b<c gives floor(c/2)+2>floor((2c+5)/4). For odd b with c<=b, equality with floor((t+6)/4) is equivalent to 0<=b-c<=4, including c=b separately where the extra factor raises the count by one. Equivalently the admissible odd b are in [t/2,(t+4)/2] with b<=t. For odd t there is exactly one, and for even t there are two iff t/2 is odd and t>=6; t=2 has only b=1. This proves the claimed existence and multiplicities and includes n=6. Reversing preserves the set sizes. The algebraic proof is all-parameter; the uploaded verification reports 8,820 direct factor tests and minimization via the formula at lengths 6..300, inspected but not rerun. No unrestricted five-one minimum follows.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The attained value on the four-run face and its computable equality conditions are not the new part. The extended census accounts jointly for factors using the leading and the trailing zero-runs (no Abelian square can span all five runs, because it would contain five ones). The strict bound when both outer gaps are positive rules out additional minimizers in the five-run interior. The full theorem adds this exclusion and covers degenerate run/short-length boundaries, without settling arbitrary five-one compositions.

value.rationale: The effective four-run witness motivates exactly this extension: adding a left outer zero-run to the two-plus-three witness, while moving the same total zero count among gaps, is a natural family around a known low-count construction. The all-parameter literal census and strict cost of opening both outer gaps show why that extension produces no improvement or additional extremizers. The novel value is this rigidity in the larger family, not reproducing the four-run numerical minimum or suggesting an unrestricted result.
